Report_ID: Children with persistent middle ear effusion (no resolution of any type B ear to A/C1) at 1 month
Title: An open randomised study of autoinflation in 4- to 11-year-old school children with otitis media with effusion in primary care
Author: Williamson I, Vennik J, Harnden A, Voysey M, Perera R, Breen M, et al.
Comment: Events recorded as PERSISTENCE (total minus resolved) per the synthesis plan: 131-62=69 (autoinflation) and 132-47=85 (usual care). Totals are the numbers with a 1-month outcome (131 and 132), not the 160 per arm randomised. The paper's own adjusted RR of 1.36 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.88) is for RESOLUTION, i.e. the inverse direction of the plan's persistence RR, so it was deliberately NOT entered into the risk_ratio field to avoid a direction conflict with the persistence counts. p-value 0.0582 applies to this same treatment-vs-control comparison. No design-effect adjustment needed (per-child data).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Nasal balloon autoinflation (Otovent) three times per day plus usual care') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: pragmatic two-arm open randomised controlled trial
domain: otitis media with effusion / primary care paediatrics
Participant type: School children aged 4-11 years with OME symptoms/concerns in previous 3 months and a type B tympanogram in one or both ears
Recruitment source: 43 general practices from 17 UK primary care trusts, recruited January 2012 to February 2013
Outcome measurement: Per-child persistence at 1 month, derived as total analysed minus number with normal tympanograms (resolution)
Outcome variable: Children with persistent middle ear effusion (no resolution of any type B ear to A/C1) at 1 month
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks

Report_ID: Children with persistent middle ear effusion (no resolution of any type B ear to A/C1) at 1 month
Title: An open randomised study of autoinflation in 4- to 11-year-old school children with otitis media with effusion in primary care
Author: Williamson I, Vennik J, Harnden A, Voysey M, Perera R, Breen M, et al.
Comment: Events recorded as PERSISTENCE per the synthesis plan: 9-3=6 (autoinflation) and 9-2=7 (standard care); totals are the numbers assessed at 1 month (9 per arm) rather than randomised (11 allocated to autoinflation, of whom 2 were incorrectly randomised and excluded; 10 allocated to standard care, 1 lost to follow-up). The reported OR 1.75 (95% CI 0.20 to 14.20) and difference of 11.1% (95% CI -36.0% to 58.2%) are stated in the direction of RESOLUTION, i.e. the inverse of the plan's persistence direction; M_diff is the paper's own percentage-point difference in resolution, not a persistence difference. No risk ratio was reported by the paper for the pilot. No design-effect adjustment needed (per-child data).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Nasal balloon autoinflation (Otovent) plus routine care') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: otitis media with effusion / primary care paediatrics
Participant type: School children aged 4-11 years with at least one type B tympanogram and OME-related symptoms/history
Recruitment source: Four GP practices recruited through the Primary Care Research Network (Hampshire, Wiltshire, Buckinghamshire, West Berkshire); 357 invited, 58 screened, 21 randomised
Outcome measurement: Per-child persistence at 1 month, derived as number assessed minus number resolved (Table 3)
Outcome variable: Children with persistent middle ear effusion (no resolution of any type B ear to A/C1) at 1 month
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks

Report_ID: Persistent middle ear effusion / negative pressure (type C2 or type B tympanogram) at day 30, per ear
Title: Autoinflation as a Treatment of Secretory Otitis Media — A Randomized Controlled Study
Author: Stangerup, Sederberg-Olsen, Balle
Comment: Event counts are NOT reported verbatim; they were derived from the table's reported percentages multiplied by the stated N of ears (control: (36.1%+50.8%) x 61 = 53.0 ears; autoinflation: (50.0%+26.1%) x 47 = 35.8 ears) and rounded. Unit of analysis is EARS, not children; the design-effect adjustment specified in the plan was NOT applied because the number of children contributing the 61/47 ears at day 30 is not reported (at entry the mean ears per child was 73/47 = 1.55 for control and 51/46 = 1.11 for autoinflation, implying design effects of about 1.28 and 1.05). The reported P<.05 refers to the Mann-Whitney rank-sum comparison of the full tympanogram-type distribution, not to this dichotomised proportion.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Autoinflation group (nose tube and balloon, 3 times daily for 2 weeks)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Children aged 3-10 years with secretory otitis media for at least 3 months
Recruitment source: Ear, Nose and Throat Clinic, Helsingor Hospital, Denmark
Outcome measurement: Tympanogram type C2 or B counted as persistence; derived from reported percentages x N of ears
Outcome variable: Persistent middle ear effusion / negative pressure (type C2 or type B tympanogram) at day 30, per ear
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks

Report_ID: Persistent middle ear effusion (no tympanometric resolution of >= 1 type-B ear per child) at 1 month
Title: Effect of nasal balloon autoinflation in children with otitis media with effusion in primary care: an open randomized controlled trial
Author: Williamson et al.
Comment: Paper reports RESOLUTION, not persistence; persistence computed as analysed total minus resolved (standard care 132-47=85; autoinflation 131-62=69). Per-child data used (preferred over the per-ear GEE analysis also reported in Table 3), so no design-effect adjustment was applied. The paper's own adjusted RR 1.36 (95% CI 0.99-1.88) refers to resolution (RR > 1 favours autoinflation) and is therefore NOT entered in the risk_ratio field to avoid a direction mismatch with the persistence outcome. Totals are the modified-ITT analysed Ns (131/132), not the 160/160 randomised.; excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
domain: medicine / primary care otolaryngology (otitis media with effusion)
Participant type: Children aged 4-11 years with recent ear symptoms and tympanometrically confirmed otitis media with effusion (1 or 2 type-B tympanograms)
Recruitment source: 43 general practices from 17 primary care trusts in the UK (89% identified by practice computer search)
Outcome measurement: Number of children without definite tympanometric resolution at 1 month, out of children analysed (modified intention-to-treat)
Outcome variable: Persistent middle ear effusion (no tympanometric resolution of >= 1 type-B ear per child) at 1 month
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks

Report_ID: Persistent middle ear effusion at 6 weeks (ears, design-effect adjusted)
Title: ffa45583_Ercan-et-al-2005 — Long term effect of autoinflation in the treatment of otitis media with effusion
Author: Ercan, Çakır, Kayaoğlu, Turgut
Comment: Paper reports data per EAR only (no per-child persistence). Raw persistence derived as total minus resolved: autoinflation 21/48, control 31/45. Design-effect adjustment APPLIED per synthesis plan: autoinflation mean ears/child = 48/30 = 1.6, DE = 1 + (1.6−1)×0.5 = 1.30 → 21/1.30 = 16.2 events, 48/1.30 = 36.9 total; control mean ears/child = 45/30 = 1.5, DE = 1.25 → 31/1.25 = 24.8 events, 45/1.25 = 36.0 total. Chi-square 5.95 and p=0.014 are the paper's own UNADJUSTED per-ear test of the resolution outcome. Note: control arm received nasal saline irrigation (standard care), and the autoinflation arm received the same co-intervention, so the comparison isolates autoinflation.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group 1 — autoinflation (Otovent 3x/day for 6 weeks) + nasal saline irrigation (30 children, 48 ears)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: otolaryngology / paediatrics (chronic otitis media with effusion)
Participant type: children aged 4-10 years (mean 6.2) with chronic otitis media with effusion
Recruitment source: ENT clinic, Şişli Etfal Training and Research Hospital, Istanbul (January 2002 - April 2004)
Outcome measurement: Ears with effusion still present at 6th week = total ears minus ears in which effusion had cleared (autoinflation 48 − 27 = 21/48; control 45 − 14 = 31/45), then divided by the design effect for clustering of ears within children
Outcome variable: Persistent middle ear effusion at 6 weeks (ears, design-effect adjusted)
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks
unit_of_analysis: per ear (design-effect adjusted to child level)

Report_ID: Persistent glue ear (no improvement) at 3 weeks
Title: Autoinflation in the treatment of glue ear in children
Author: Brooker & McNeice
Comment: Data reported per ear only (Group A 37/41 no improvement; Group B 27/37 no improvement; 78 ears from 40 children). Per the synthesis plan, a design-effect adjustment was applied: average ears per child = 78/40 = 1.95, design effect = 1 + (1.95 - 1) x 0.5 = 1.475; events and totals were divided by 1.475 (A: 37/41 -> 25.1/27.8; B: 27/37 -> 18.3/25.1). Raw verbatim counts are in the evidence quote. The chi-square (3.94) and P (0.047) are the paper's own unadjusted per-ear test. Outcome definition is improvement in audiogram or tympanogram peak rather than tympanogram type B/C2 alone.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group A (autoinflation)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: children aged 3-10 years (mean 5.7) with unilateral or bilateral glue ear
Recruitment source: Audiology Clinic, Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children
Outcome measurement: Number of ears with no improvement out of total glue ears per group (design-effect adjusted to approximate per-child units)
Outcome variable: Persistent glue ear (no improvement) at 3 weeks
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks
unit_of_analysis: per ear (design-effect adjusted to child level)

Report_ID: Ears with persistent middle ear effusion (non-responders) at four weeks
Title: Autoinflation for treatment of persistent otitis media with effusion in children: A cross-over study with a 12-month follow-up
Author: Bidarian-Moniri, Ramos, Ejnell
Comment: Data reported PER EAR, all children bilateral. Raw counts: Group A 8 non-responder ears of 44 ears (40 type B + 4 type C2 at inclusion, Table 1); Group B 42 non-responder ears (41 unchanged + 1 deteriorated) of 46 ears (42 type B + 4 type C2, Table 1). Design-effect adjustment APPLIED: average ears per child = 2, design effect = 1 + (2-1) x 0.5 = 1.5; events and totals divided by 1.5 (Group A 8/1.5=5.33 of 44/1.5=29.33; Group B 42/1.5=28 of 46/1.5=30.67). 'Improved to C2' was counted as resolution/improvement per the synthesis plan's rule. No between-group test statistic for this comparison is reported by the paper.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group A - autoinflation device, four weeks of home treatment') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: children aged 2-8 years with persistent bilateral OME (type B or C2 tympanogram >=3 months) awaiting grommet surgery
Recruitment source: ENT out-patient clinics, Sahlgrenska University Hospital (Sweden) and Centro Hospitalar do Algarve (Portugal)
Outcome measurement: Number of ears not showing tympanometric normalisation or improvement at four weeks (total ears minus responders), design-effect adjusted to child level
Outcome variable: Ears with persistent middle ear effusion (non-responders) at four weeks
outcome_family: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks
unit_of_analysis: per ear (design-effect adjusted to child level)
